page.layout: One printed page (left) with a main text column; a narrow strip of text at the right edge belonging to the facing page, cut off, treated as the right page's column. Left page: running text, a heading "X.", a section break, a chapter heading "CAP. III", a sub-title and a paragraph beginning with a large initial. Right edge: fragments of the facing page's text, not transcribed as main text.

main_text.p: do contra Dei regnum & creatu-rarum reliquarum salutem efficere ipsi Deus concedit, summâ cum voluptate patrat; quia nil sibi convenientius & suâ indole dignius concipere potest.
main_text.head: X.
main_text.p: Talis igitur Genius malus, aut potius innumerabiles tales (quia probabile satis est ipso naturæ lumine, quòd quemadodum in omni rebellione fit, multi defecerint, à Duce & authore illius factionis in consortium culpæ & solatium poenæ contracti) tales, inquam, Genii mali, si igitur ponantur in rerum natura existere, quidnam in corpora & per corpora efficere valeant Deo ipsis libertatem concedente (juxta th. 3. c. 1.) indagandum erit.
main_text.head: CAP. III. De potentia malorum Angelorum in corpora Generaliter.
main_text.p: Corpora quæ ministerio Diaboli inservire apta sunt, in genere quidem sunt omnia fluida, quia motum inse jam habent, extra quem nihil efficiet,

page.notes: Right edge strip shows cut-off words of the facing page (for example "ciet", "ipsi", "nat", "nut", "cat"); these are partial and not transcribed. Some words in the left column are doubtful at the ink smudges (e.g. "quòd", "insejam" read as "infe jam"), marked as read. A small mark "*" stands beside the paragraph starting "Talis", not a note.
